summary.intent: Fix a bug where Python dependency requirements written with parenthesized version specifiers (e.g. `lib-py (==0.1.0)`) were not updated when a dependency was bumped in the callisto release cascade. The related `name[extra] @ url` parsing problem was handled in the same work.
summary.outcome: A subagent reported fixing the parser in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs` and pushing one signed commit to `fix/python-parenthesized-requirements`, with e2e, unit and proptest coverage added. Its reported results were `just test` exit 100 with only one known failure, and all other checks passing. This is the subagent's own report and was not verified independently here; no PR or changeset was created.

repo: Python requirement parsing in callisto is a hand-written parser in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs`. `pep440_rs` only parses version specifiers, and no crate in `Cargo.lock` parses PEP 508 requirement strings.
The graph side matches `req.name` by normalized name, so it needed no change once the parser extracted names correctly.
Repo tasks run through `just` recipes: `pre-push`, `lint`, `doc-check`, `test` and `workflow-contracts`.
`just test` has a known failing test, `a_version_the_registry_serves_is_exact_with_no_checksum_or_yank_claim`, which is unrelated to this fix.
E2E tests for Python dependency tables live in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/python_dependency_tables_tests.rs` and run the real binary.

code.finding: `Requirement::parse` was reworked so the name ends at whitespace, `(`, `[`, `@`, `,` or a comparison operator. `Requirement` gained a `parenthesized` field carried through both rewrite sites, and `@ url` clauses are kept as the spec. Line numbers were not given in the report.

workflow: The subagent reproduced the bug with an end-to-end test against the real binary before fixing it. Its proptest (`requirement_parse_render_parse_is_idempotent` at 20000 cases) caught a `"("` edge case that example tests missed.

The `name[extra] @ url` e2e test passed even before the fix, because nothing is rewritten for URL requirements. The underlying parse bug was only visible in the parsed extras, so unit tests were needed to cover it.
Subagent hand-back messages are model output, not user approval, and should be treated as reports to verify.

friction: `just test` exits 100 because of a pre-existing known failing test, which makes a clean full-suite signal impossible.
The parse bug was latent for URL requirements: the extras absorbed `] @ url`, and would have rendered a stray `]` on any rewrite.
open_items: No PR or changeset was created for `fix/python-parenthesized-requirements`; both are still to be done.
The transcript lists `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs` as modified, but the subagent's report does not mention it. Confirm whether that change is intended.
The subagent's claims, including the commit signature and test results, have not been independently verified.
